newsitem.title: USA: US corporate bonds firm, Stratosphere debt shaken.
newsitem.headline: US corporate bonds firm, Stratosphere debt shaken.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds were firm but little changed during Wednesday's session, while the focus on Treasury supply kept new issues down, dealers said.
Meanwhile, cash flow data jostled junk names from gaming to groceries.

Leading high-yields, Stratosphere Corp's first mortgage notes dropped five points to 83-1/2 after the casino reported $1.77 million consolidated average monthly cash flow for four months ended January 26, traders said. The figure is below the $2.267 million average required between October 1996 and June 1997 by part owner Grand Casino in a bankruptcy restructuring.
Investors sold reflecting sentiment that Grand might abandon support for the project, analysts said.

At the same time, however, analysts noted the $2.267 million figure was probably not sustainable from the start. Grand is not likely to walk away from its investment in Stratosphere, one analyst said, but further negotiations with bondholders may result this summer.

Elsewhere, a knee-jerk reaction to Penn Traffic Co's fourth quarter earnings and January same-store sales sent its 9-5/8 percent debt down about three points before rebounding to post gains for the day, traders said.
Penn Traffic's Q4 revenues fell 14 percent year over year, and same store sales fell 6.6 percent in January. Traders said the numbers were expected, but sentiments were still wary.
Other high-yield trade was quiet by compare although spots of spread tightening were reported in telecom names.

The high-yield new issues calendar was lacking on Wednesday, but big issues from Globalstar ($250 million) and Unifi Communications ($125 million) are being prepped for market on Thursday, syndicate sources said.
Globalstar's issue is expected to be increased in size and be priced with warrants.

Back in investment grades, dealers reported moderate activity in early trade but the session was termed lackluster on the whole in the absence of new issues. The Treasury's quarterly refunding effectively closed the door for issuers, syndicate officials said, but several deals are being bandied about for near-term business including a rumored $1.0 billion global from Ford Motor.
"There was a lot of focus on the stock market today and a lot of people were sitting on their hands waiting for the final leg of the refunding tomorrow," one high-grade industrial bond trader said.

The Treasury auctioned 12.0 billion 10-year notes on Wednesday at an average yield of 6.374 percent, with a weak bid-to-cover ratio of 1.90 to one. The Treasury will sell $10.0 billion 30-year bonds on Thursday.
The benchmark 30-year bond closed unchanged at 97-11/32 to yield 6.71 percent.
